newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey central bank sold $1 bln in last two weeks.
newsitem.headline: Turkey central bank sold $1 bln in last two weeks.

text.p: Turkish central bank sold $1 billion from November 4 to 15 to curb dollar demand, according to the central bank's balance sheet released on Thursday.
The figures showed that the bank's net foreign currency position fell by $1 billion and produced a $600 million short position.
But the bank's foreign currency reserves showed only a $75 million drop $17.2 billion in the two-week period due to an increase of $950 million in foreign currency liabilities.
The rise in foreign currency liabilities was due to the Treasury's $900 million worth dollar and mark-denominated, three-year bond issue to Turkish banks which was finalised last week.
Turkish banks' dollar demand rose in the last two weeks due higher inflation expectations and purchases to cover short currency positions ahead of the year-end.

The central bank raised its overnight bid and offer rates to 55-80 percent on Wednesday from previous 50-75 percent to support the lira after frequent interventions since early November to restrain demand for the U.S. currency.
Banks began selling dollars for lira in the last two days after the overnight money rates went up, bankers said.
